title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at roughly half the price of GPT-5.6
bullets.summary: Released 22 Sep: Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 per Mtok as permanent pricing, with OpenAI claiming Sol makes about half as many factual mistakes as its predecessor; live in API, Codex and ChatGPT.
bullets.how: Luna is a cheap candidate for high-volume Construct batch work (alt text, classification); for PRAGMA, a new model tier to re-measure client visibility against.

bullets.title: Baselayer raises $35M Series A (M13) and launches 'Know Your Agent' identity for AI agents
bullets.summary: Announced 22 Sep: the bank identity-verification vendor's Agentic Identity Suite checks who deployed an agent, who it represents and whether it may transact.
bullets.how: Signals that agent identity/authorization is becoming buyer-facing infrastructure; a PRAGMA talking point for clients letting agents act on their behalf. No direct B9 use.

bullets.title: arXiv 2609.15906: Authorization Architectures for Tool-Using AI Agents
bullets.summary: September paper laying out a principal hierarchy (user, operator, orchestrator, sub-agent, tool endpoint) and five layers: identity/credentials, delegation and scope propagation, runtime enforcement, prompt injection as authorization bypass, and auditability.
bullets.how: A ready checklist for The Construct's credential-bearing skills and Hermes loops: scope what each sub-agent inherits and log it.

praxis_lesson: Two of today's three items are about the same thing, agents acting with borrowed authority. As model prices keep halving, the scarce layer for The Construct is scoping and auditing what each agent is allowed to do, not the model underneath it.
